intro: Fixed windows turn irregular event times into an aligned count series. Half-open intervals assign a boundary event to exactly one window.
task: Aggregate event counts into half-open integer windows anchored at a supplied origin.
requirements: timestamps is a sequence of integers; width is an integer 1..1000000000 and origin is an integer. Return sorted [window_start,count] pairs for occupied half-open windows [start,start+width), where start=origin+floor((t-origin)/width)*width. Negative timestamps are valid.
Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Integer inputs must be Python ints, excluding bool, within the task-specific bounds or -1e9..1e9 when no narrower bounds are stated.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Floor division handles negative offsets correctly; truncation toward zero does not.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Count occupied windows, then sort their start values.

explanation: Fixed windows turn irregular event times into an aligned count series. Half-open intervals assign a boundary event to exactly one window.
An origin shifts the entire grid without changing its width. Empty windows are deliberately omitted so sparse event streams stay compact.
